specification_compliance: r1 F1 is addressed. globals.css:1278-1282 now places `.justified-grid > .justified-grid-cell { transition-property: none; }` inside `@layer base`. globals.css:1 is `@import "tailwindcss"`, which fixes the layer order as theme, base, components, utilities. ArchiveEntryCard's `transition-colors` (ArchiveEntryCard.tsx:116) is in `utilities`, so it now beats this rule. The unlayered `[data-flip="invert"]` and `[data-flip="play"]` rules at globals.css:1286-1296 also still beat it, so the FLIP fade and zoom keep working.
r1 F3 is addressed. frontend/src/hooks/__tests__/useJustifiedHold.test.tsx is the planned jsdom test of the hold hook's branching, as listed in the touch points.

Moving the rule leaves held cells' behaviour unchanged: JustifiedFileCell.tsx:74 carries no transition utility (only relative, opacity-40, opacity-50 and select-none), so for FileGrid cells the base-layer `none` is still the property in effect. Archive cells are never held, because ArchiveEntryGrid does not call useJustifiedHold, and `transition-colors` does not include `visibility`.

archiveJustifiedCells.test.tsx:212-216 reads the first `.justified-grid > .justified-grid-cell {` block, which is still the layout rule at globals.css:1239. Inside @layer, the moved rule is indented and comes later in the file, so it does not shadow that match.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Inherited from r1 and unchanged in this commit: useJustifiedFlip now plays a fade for released cells on the `before.width !== width` path, which previously never animated. The I5 e2e case 'an append after the grid resized with no commit' pins this path.
regression_risks: The base-layer `transition-property: none` now yields to any Tailwind transition utility on a justified cell. If someone later adds `transition` or `transition-all` to JustifiedFileCell, `visibility` would transition again. Without reduced motion, a newly held cell would then stay painted for the utility's duration (visible→hidden flips at the end), which would break I1/I8's 'before the next paint'. No test pins that JustifiedFileCell has no such utility, apart from the class lists in the fixture parity test.
The hook order in FileGrid (flip before hold) is still enforced only by a comment. This is unchanged from r1.
test_coverage: New e2e-layout case (justified-grid.spec.ts:411-419) checks that the archive openable cell's computed transition-property contains background-color. It would fail if the rule were moved back out of the layer, so it kills a revert of the F1 fix. It does not appear in the generated `registered` list, and it is not a generated case, so the 'every generated case was registered' test is unaffected.

useJustifiedHold.test.tsx mutation reasoning: dropping `moreMayFollow` from the signature, or from applyHold, is killed by the I6 test. Dropping `--jg-ratio` from cellSignature is killed by the I8 ratio test: the guard would return early and leave [d,e] where [c,d,e] is expected. Dropping the `cells[0].offsetTop !== lastTop` guard is killed by the I7 test. Removing the focus move is killed by the I2 test. Removing the `if (target)` skip, or the held-skip in the backwards walk, is killed by the 'skips earlier cells' test (b is expected, not c or d).

The I9 jsdom test survives deleting the signature guard altogether, because recomputing gives the same held set. The guard is a cost optimisation that the spec explicitly does not make an invariant, so this is acceptable.

Nothing kills deleting the base-layer `transition-property: none` rule. Under reduced motion, its only effect is a 0.01ms `visibility` transition, which is not observable within a frame. The rule therefore has no test that would fail without it.

trajectory: The r2 fix round (5f7e3e9a; cf1dcd17 and 1fce81d6 are docs-only) adds no branch, state or prediction to the runtime code. It moves one existing CSS rule into `@layer base`, which narrows that rule's reach rather than adding a condition. It also adds tests: a jsdom suite for useJustifiedHold's existing branches and one e2e-layout assertion. r1 had no earlier fix round to compare against. Nothing suggests the design is being patched: no new guard, no new marker attribute and no new special case was introduced in response to r1.
